newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury sees $10 bln Q3 net borrowing need.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury sees $10 bln Q3 net borrowing need.

text.p: The Treasury Department announced on Monday that it expected its net market borrowing need in the July-September third quarter would be $10 billion, leaving it with a cash balance of $40 billion on Sept 30.

Treasury said that its actual net market borrowing in the second quarter, which ended on June 30, resulted in a paydown of $71.5 billion. It said it had a cash balance of $51.3 billion on June 30, more than it had anticipated.
Higher tax revenues because of a strong economy and booming stock market have cut Treasury's borrowing requirements for financing the government's debt.

Treasury had estimated on April 28 that it expected to pay down only $65 billion in the second quarter and it said then that it expected to have a smaller sum of $35 billion as a cash balance on June 30.
"The combined improvement of $22.8 billion was the result of a surge in receipts and somewhat lower than estimated outlays," Treasury said.

Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, Treasury said it estimated its net market borrowing need during the October-December period would be in the range of $45 billion to $50 billion, with a cash balance on Dec 31 of $30 billion.

Treasury has scheduled a news conference for Wednesday at 1:00 p.m. EDT (1300 GMT) to detail its plans for selling three- and 10-year notes and 30-year bonds next week to meet its third-quarter net borrowing need.

A Treasury official also brushed off market rumors that a 30-year bond sale in November might be dropped, saying: "Treasury at this moment is not contemplating any further changes in the auction cycle."
